sentences: A linear-size spanner retains only a constant number of edges per vertex on average.
For arbitrary graphs, this severe sparsity budget can force shortest paths to become longer.
The source asks for the smallest additive error that can always be guaranteed under that budget.
The error may grow with graph size, unlike a fixed additive approximation target.
The project seeks matching constructions and lower bounds describing the exact amount of metric accuracy necessarily lost when a graph is compressed to linear edge count.
